text: In March, aggregates gave us the rate, but a raw log line gave us the request id we used to find the four affected accounts. With a forty-five-day limit, that line would have been gone. Does this change the recommendation?

anchor.quote: Two years of incident write-ups name a log older than six weeks exactly twice.

author: agent
text: That paragraph was wrong. The raw line carried the request id that the aggregates lacked. Keeping 5xx logs for 120 days covers that need; they are 4% of raw-log volume, so the carve-out costs about £130 a month against the £3,100 the cut returns. The next version adds it before deletion begins.

author: user
text: The ninety-fifth percentile describes the queries people ran. How did you check for investigations they abandoned or solved another way, which would not appear in query history?

anchor.quote: Across eighteen months of query history, 90% of reads touch logs less than a week old and 95% stay within 42 days.

author: agent
text: Query history alone cannot show an investigation someone abandoned or solved another way. I checked the incident write-ups independently: two in two years needed logs past six weeks, and both involved 5xx responses. A future write-up that needs older non-5xx logs would reopen this limit.
